result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a multi-lane roadway passing under a concrete overpass, with sidewalks provided on both sides. While a signalized intersection with marked crosswalks is visible ahead, the underpass creates significant shadows and visual obstructions from structural piers.

hazards.name: Underpass Shadowing
hazards.description: The overpass creates deep shadows that can reduce the visibility of pedestrians to drivers, especially when transitioning from bright sunlight.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground under the bridge structure

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Piers
hazards.description: Large concrete bridge supports can block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles approaching the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway under the overpass

interventions.title: Under-bridge Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian-scale lighting under the overpass to eliminate dark spots and improve personal security and visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at the intersection ahead to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse crosswalk markings to high-visibility continental or ladder patterns.

result.summary: The image shows a pedestrian crossing area within a transit station environment, situated beneath an elevated rail structure. While sidewalks and a marked crosswalk are present, the environment is characterized by faded pavement markings and visual obstructions from structural pillars.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Structural Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Support pillars for the elevated rail structure create blind spots between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crossing with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Actuated Warning System
interventions.description: Install Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFBs) to alert drivers when pedestrians are crossing in this high-activity transit zone.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Structure Lighting
interventions.description: Improve lighting levels beneath the elevated tracks to eliminate dark shadows and improve nighttime visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is located under an elevated structure with a wide zebra-marked crosswalk. A massive concrete support pillar creates a severe visual obstruction at the sidewalk edge, and the area suffers from deep shadows that reduce visibility.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from bridge pillar
hazards.description: The large concrete pillar at the edge of the sidewalk blocks the view between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching vehicles.

hazards.name: Poor lighting and deep shadows
hazards.description: The area under the elevated structure is heavily shadowed, reducing the visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: Extend the curb around the pillar to move the pedestrian waiting area into the line of sight of drivers.

interventions.title: Enhanced Pedestrian Lighting
interventions.description: Install high-intensity LED lighting under the bridge structure to illuminate the crosswalk and sidewalk areas.

interventions.title: Advanced Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install pedestrian crossing signs with flashing beacons before the bridge to alert drivers of the crossing.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian signals. The environment is characterized by large-scale institutional structures like a parking garage and an overhead walkway, which provide a wide but somewhat sterile walking environment with potential sightline obstructions from structural pillars.

hazards.name: Structural pillars
hazards.description: Large pillars for the overhead walkway are located near the curb, potentially obstructing sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The intersection corner appears to have a wide radius, which may allow vehicles to make turns at higher speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and reduce vehicle turning speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install additional lighting under the overhead structure to ensure pedestrians remain visible in shadowed areas.
